clue.text: Bill gets acknowledgment in the minutes

definitions.note: the Latin plural word is used for recorded proceedings or minutes

parts.note: AC is the abbreviation for account, a bill to be paid
TA is the British informal word of thanks, a small acknowledgment

explanation.surface: A piece of legislation earns a mention in the record of a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a parliamentary bill, but it is an account. TA is British slang for 'thank you'.
explanation.definitionFit: Acta is Latin for things done, used in English for the official record of proceedings, much like minutes.

clue.text: See 22
Needing a large collar like Europa, perhaps

definitions.text: Needing a large collar like Europa, perhaps

parts.words: Needing a large collar like Europa, perhaps
parts.note: a thick-throated person needs a big collar; in myth Europa rode on the neck of Zeus disguised as a bull, so she too was, playfully, joined to a beefy neck

explanation.surface: A tailor's remark that a mythical princess needs an outsized collar.
explanation.walkthrough: Europa was carried off by Zeus in the form of a bull; the clue jokes that she, perched on that neck, is described by the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a thick, short, powerful neck like a bull's would need a large shirt collar.

clue.text: Place surrounded … surrounded by … by … marksmen?

definitions.text: Place surrounded … surrounded by … by … marksmen?

indicators.note: surrounded by tells us one piece is enclosed within the other, here the word by

parts.note: taken as written
an isle is a place, a piece of land

explanation.surface: A stammering description of a spot ringed by sharpshooters.
explanation.walkthrough: The stammer in the clue supplies the word by twice, and 'surrounded' tells you which way round they go. The answer is the Surrey range where the National Rifle Association shoots.
explanation.definitionFit: Bisley in Surrey is the British centre for target rifle shooting, a place full of marksmen.

clue.text: Writer's family goods: a field day (part 1) is following

parts.note: kin means family
GS is taken as a short form of goods
a ley is a field under grass
the first part of the day is the morning, AM
taken as written, and following places it after the earlier pieces

explanation.surface: A family's possessions and a day out in the fields make up a writer's estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is following' just puts the word is at the end. 'day (part 1)' means the morning, the first half of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Kingsley Amis was the English novelist whose books are the theme of this puzzle.

clue.text: See 5
On the contrary, not a single one undesirable to Hitler

indicators.note: taking the contrary of the word On here means reading it backwards

parts.note: taken as written before being turned
nary means not a single, as in nary a word
an is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: An emphatic denial that even a single person was unwelcome to Hitler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the contrary' turns ON into NO. 'Nary' is dialect for not one.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nazis regarded anyone of non-Aryan descent as undesirable, so the phrase describes such a person.

clue.text: Listen! Listen! 5 6 liked it

indicators.note: the second Listen! tells us to attend to the sound of the first one

parts.note: hear is a command to listen

explanation.surface: Repeated calls for attention, then a remark that an author enjoyed something.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition completes the title of the Kingsley Amis novel I Like It Here; 'Hear! Hear!' is also the parliamentary cheer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amis novel title I Like It Here ends with this word, so the author liked it in that place.

clue.text: Composer for clarinet's first man — disaster engulfs second one

indicators.note: first means take the opening letter of clarinet's

parts.note: he is a man

indicators.note: engulfs means the word for disaster swallows the letter for second

parts.note: ruin is a disaster
B is the second letter, or second class
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A composer writing for the clarinet suffers a disaster involving his second piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second' is B, as in second-rate grade B.
explanation.definitionFit: Luigi Cherubini was an Italian composer of operas and church music who worked in Paris.

clue.text: Deer gives tongue with energy

parts.note: a cow gives tongue when it moos
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A deer cries out vigorously.
explanation.definitionFit: The moose is the largest species of the deer family.

clue.text: See 27
Member isn't in time to do his job

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body
something that is late is not in time

explanation.surface: A member of parliament arrives too late to do his work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' reads as an MP but gives LEG, a limb; yet an MP's job is exactly to make laws.
explanation.definitionFit: Making laws is the work of a legislator, so to pass laws is a member's job.

clue.text: 23 semiprecious bird holding back agents

indicators.note: holding means the bird's name contains the other piece

parts.note: the jay is a bird of the crow family

indicators.note: back means the word for agents is read in reverse

parts.note: reps, short for representatives, are sales agents

explanation.surface: A bird clutches some agents, all described as semi-precious and opaque.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 is the answer to 23-down, OPAQUE; jasper is an opaque semi-precious stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Jasper is an opaque semi-precious quartz, so something resembling it is opaque and semi-precious.

clue.text: 5 6's filmed bird unconvincing in a car

indicators.note: in means the bird and the thin piece go inside the car

parts.note: a Jag is a Jaguar car
Kes is the film about a boy and his kestrel
a thin excuse is unconvincing

explanation.surface: A novelist's filmed bird looks feeble sitting in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: KES is Ken Loach's 1969 film about a boy and a kestrel; JAG is a Jaguar. The answer is the Amis novel Jake's Thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Jake's Thing is a 1978 comic novel by Kingsley Amis, so it is one of his works.

clue.text: See 27
Siegfried's wife (cream, not brown?) turned red like him

definitions.note: the question jokes that she is cream-hilde, not brown-hilde, i.e. not Wagner's Brünnhilde

indicators.note: turned means the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A note on Siegfried's wife blushing red like her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: In Wagner Siegfried weds Brünnhilde ('brown'); in the Nibelungenlied his wife is the 'cream' one, Kriemhild. 'turned' rearranges RED LIKE HIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Kriemhild is Siegfried's wife in the medieval German epic the Nibelungenlied.

clue.text: In the Sun we try to be dry

indicators.note: In tells us the answer lies inside the run of words Sun we try

explanation.surface: Out in the sunshine, we attempt to stay dry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not wet is dry, a straight synonym.

clue.text: A peasant sounds indifferent to a king

indicators.note: sounds tells us to say the words aloud

parts.note: cool means indifferent, then A, then K for king, giving cool-a-K

explanation.surface: A peasant seems unmoved by a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cool a K' said aloud matches the Russian word.
explanation.definitionFit: A kulak was a relatively prosperous Russian peasant farmer, persecuted under Stalin.

clue.text: 5 6's juicy milk shake's a one-off

indicators.note: a shake rearranges the letters
off means a letter is removed

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A novelist's juicy milkshake is a single treat.
explanation.walkthrough: JUICY MILK loses an I ('a one-off') and the rest is rearranged into the Amis novel Lucky Jim.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucky Jim, published in 1954, was Kingsley Amis's first and most famous novel.

clue.text: Money's sound in 23

parts.note: 23-down is pronounced oh-PAKE, and its middle syllable is the noise meant

explanation.surface: Money's noise lies inside something unclear.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 is OPAQUE, pronounced oh-PAKE: its middle sound is the word for wages.
explanation.definitionFit: Pay is money received as wages.

clue.text: It's cheap, being composed of others' work

indicators.note: being composed suggests the letters are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: A dismissive remark that something is cheap because it is copied from other artists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being composed' rearranges IT'S CHEAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastiche is a work imitating or patched together from the work of other artists.

clue.text: See 26
Leaves the church taking seat outside

indicators.note: the seat takes the church inside it

parts.note: sedes is the Latin word for seat, as in the Holy See, here on the outside
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone leaves the church while occupying a seat outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves the church' looks like the whole definition, but 'the church' is wordplay. The seat is the Latin word, as in the Holy See (Sancta Sedes).
explanation.definitionFit: To secede is to withdraw formally from a body, so it means leaves.

clue.text: Break not fatal, if you're up before ten

definitions.text: Break not fatal, if you're up before ten

parts.words: Break not fatal, if you're up before ten
parts.note: a boxer floored and up before the count of ten is not knocked out, which suggests a pause in play

explanation.surface: A boxer's knockdown is survivable if they rise before the count of ten.
explanation.walkthrough: In boxing a floored fighter is out if not up by the count of ten; the answer read as two words says the fall was not fatal.
explanation.definitionFit: A time-out is a short break called during a game or match.

clue.text: 5 6's man has informed about many problems

indicators.note: about means the word for informed goes around the man

parts.note: told means informed
he is a man
D is the Roman numeral 500, many
evils are problems or troubles

explanation.surface: A novelist's character has learned of many difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: D (500) for 'many' is a crossword convention. The answer is the Booker-winning Amis novel The Old Devils.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Devils won Kingsley Amis the Booker Prize in 1986.

clue.text: Work on a problem off-line that's unfathomable

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: off means the following letters are removed

parts.note: a query is a question or problem
RY is short for railway, a line

explanation.surface: Someone works on a puzzle away from the internet, finding it baffling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off-line' tells us to take the railway line RY off QUERY, leaving QUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Opaque can mean hard to understand, so obscure or unfathomable.

clue.text: Setter's poem sent back in part from palace to castle

indicators.note: in means the reversed piece sits inside the word for part

parts.note: a role is a part in a play

indicators.note: sent back means the setter's poem is read backwards

parts.note: the setter would say I'm, I am
a lay is a narrative poem

explanation.surface: The crossword setter's verse is returned for being partial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns IMLAY into YALMI, which goes inside ROLE. The ROYAL MILE is the Edinburgh street from Holyrood Palace to the Castle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Mile runs between Holyrood Palace and Edinburgh Castle, so the clue describes its route.

clue.text: Hamelin's problem the resurrection of the body?

annotationWithheld.why: Hamelin's problem the resurrection of the body? (4): RAT is Hamelin's problem, but no parse found for what 'the resurrection of the body?' contributes to RATE
annotationWithheld.clue: Hamelin's problem the resurrection of the body?

clue.text: Identification to get on-line is pointless

indicators.note: pointless means a compass point is dropped

parts.note: to log on is to get online

explanation.surface: You need ID to go online, which is futile.
explanation.walkthrough: N is north, a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: A logo is an emblem that identifies a company or brand.

clue.text: 5 6's pale bird splitting in cry of pain

indicators.note: splitting means the pale bird goes between the letters of in

parts.note: taken as written
wan means pale
the tit is a small bird
ow is a cry of pain

explanation.surface: A novelist's pale bird breaks in with a cry of pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'splitting' means the pale bird cuts the word in open. The answer is an Amis novel, published in 1968.
explanation.definitionFit: I Want It Now is a 1968 novel by Kingsley Amis.

clue.text: 5 6's confused Kylie with Kali — outrage!

indicators.note: confused tells us the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A novelist muddles a pop star with a Hindu goddess, causing outrage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' rearranges KYLIE, KALI and OUTRAGE. The answer is the Amis novel Take a Girl Like You.
explanation.definitionFit: Take a Girl Like You is a 1960 novel by Kingsley Amis.

clue.text: See 13 down
50% full or empty? Betwixt and between

definitions.meaning: a glass half full or half empty has had half its contents consumed
neither sober nor fully inebriated, somewhere in the middle

explanation.definitionFit: A glass with half its drink taken is half-drunk; a person partly tipsy is also half-drunk, in between.
